chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu al-Khazraj al-Ansari, from Ali ibn Ghurab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Accursed is the one who throws his burden upon the people.'

key_terms.كَلّ: Burden, dependency, impediment — the weight one imposes on others by being unwilling to work or be self-sufficient
key_terms.مَلْعُون: Accursed, cut off from divine mercy — one of the strongest censures in prophetic speech

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about someone who imposes their burden on others?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates a prophetic declaration cursing those who impose their financial burden and dependency on others rather than earning their own livelihood. The Prophet's use of the term 'mala'un' (accursed, cut off from God's mercy) signals this is among the gravest moral failings. In the context of early Islamic society, where community solidarity was paramount, the hadith addressed the danger of exploiting communal generosity — making others bear one's worldly burdens without necessity was considered a form of social transgression.
